source.author: stat
source.text: quin socium coiisse animas et corpore in uno stare omnes, ita cuncta replet, non ullius aetas, non cultus, non forma movet; pugnantibus idem supplicibusque furit; non quisquam obsistere contra, non belli temptare vices: procul arma furentis terribilesque iubas et frontem cassidis horrent.
source.text_original: quin socium coiisse animas et corpore in uno / stare omnes, ita cuncta replet, non ullius aetas, / non cultus, non forma movet; pugnantibus idem / supplicibusque furit; non quisquam obsistere contra, / non belli temptare vices: procul arma furentis / terribilesque iubas et frontem cassidis horrent.
source.text_english: Indeed, as if the souls of the comrades had come together and all stood in a single body, so he fills everything that neither the age, nor dress, nor appearance of anyone moves him; against fighters and suppliants alike he rages; no one dares to stand against him, no one to try the fortunes of war: from afar the arms of the madman and his dreadful crests and the brow of his helmet are feared.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: hic vates Phoebique fides non vana parentis Mopsus, puniceo cui circumfusa cothurno palla imos ferit alba pedes vittataque fronte cassis et in summo laurus Peneia cono.
reuse.text_original: hic vates Phoebique fides non vana parentis / Mopsus, puniceo cui circumfusa cothurno / palla imos ferit alba pedes vittataque fronte / cassis et in summo laurus Peneia cono.
reuse.text_english: Here is that seer, and the trustworthy, no-false son of Phoebus, Mopsus, around whom a scarlet cloak hangs, striking his feet at the bottom; on his brow a helmet bound with ribbons, and on the top of the crest the Peneian laurel.
